source_text: Ὁ ἔπαρχος λέγει πρὸς Ἰουστῖνον· Ἄκουε ὁ λεγόμενος λόγιος καὶ νομίζων ἀληθινοὺς εἰδέναι λόγους· ἐὰν μαστιγωθεὶς ἀποκεφαλισθῇς, πέπεισαι ὅτι μέλλεις ἀναβαίνειν εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν; Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Ἐλπίζω ἕξειν αὐτοῦ τὰ δόγματα, ἐὰν ὑπομείνω ταῦτα. Οἶδα γὰρ πᾶσι τοῖς οὕτω βιώσασι παραμένειν τὸ θεῖον χάρισμα μέχρι τῆς ἐκπληρώσεως τοῦ παντὸς κόσμου. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπε· Σὺ οὖν ὑπονοεῖς ὅτι ἀναβήσῃ εἰς τοὺς οὐρανοὺς ἀμοιβάς τινας ἀποληψόμενος; Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Οὐχ ὑπονοῶ, ἀλλ' ἐπίσταμαι καὶ πεπληροφόρημαι. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Τὸ λοιπὸν ἔλθωμεν εἰς τὸ προκείμενον καὶ κατεπεῖγον πρᾶγμα. Συνελθόντες οὖν ὁμαθυμαδὸν θύσατε τοῖς θεοῖς. Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Οὐδεὶς εὐφρονῶν ἀπὸ εὐσεβείας ἀσεβείᾳ εἰσπίπτει. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Εἰ μὴ πείθεσθε, τιμωρηθήσεσθε ἀνηλεῶς. Ἰουστῖνος εἶπε· Δι' εὐχῆς ἔχομεν διὰ τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν τιμωρηθέντες σωθῆναι· ὅτι τοῦτο ἡμῖν σωτηρία καὶ παῤῥησία γενήσεται ἐπὶ τοῦ φοβερωτέρου καὶ παγκοσμίου βήματος τοῦ Δεσπότου ἡμῶν καὶ Σωτῆρος. Ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ μάρτυρες εἶπον· Ποίει ὃ θέλεις· ἡμεῖς γὰρ Χριστιανοί ἐσμεν, καὶ εἰδώλοις οὐ θύομεν.
thought_title: The hope of heaven and the command to sacrifice
orientation: The prefect Rusticus has finished questioning the companions individually and now turns back to Justin, pressing him on whether he really expects to go to heaven after execution, then orders the whole group to sacrifice together.
pass_a_gloss: The prefect says to Justin: Hear, [you] the [one] called learned and thinking [you] know true words: if, having been scourged, you are beheaded, are you persuaded that you are about to go up into heaven? Justin said: I hope to have his teachings, if I endure these things. For I know that to all who have lived thus the divine gift remains until the completion of the whole world. Rusticus the prefect said: Do you then suppose that you will go up into the heavens, [as one] about to receive some rewards? Justin said: I do not suppose, but I know and have been fully assured. Rusticus the prefect said: For the rest, let us come to the matter set before [us] and pressing. Having come together therefore with one accord, sacrifice to the gods. Justin said: No one of sound mind falls from worship into impiety. Rusticus the prefect said: If you do not obey, you will be punished without mercy. Justin said: We hold [it] as a prayer, having been punished for the sake of our Lord Jesus Christ, to be saved; because this will become for us salvation and boldness before the more fearful and universal tribunal of our Master and Savior. Likewise also the remaining martyrs said: Do what you wish; for we are Christians, and to idols we do not sacrifice.

choices.english: Hear, you who are called learned
choices.why: The participle λεγόμενος is passive ('called') and λόγιος means 'learned' or 'eloquent'; the address is ironic from Rusticus.
rejected: Hear, you who are said to be wise

choices.why: Perfect passive of πείθω, asking about a settled conviction, not a mere opinion.

choices.english: I hope to have his teachings
choices.why: ἕξειν is future infinitive of ἔχω ('to have'); δόγματα is the glossary term 'teaching'; 'his' refers to God or Christ, the one whose teachings Justin follows.
rejected: I hope to possess his doctrines
I hope I will receive his dogmas

choices.term: Οὐχ ὑπονοῶ, ἀλλ' ἐπίσταμαι καὶ πεπληροφόρημαι
choices.english: I do not suppose, but I know and have been fully assured
choices.why: Justin contrasts mere supposition (ὑπονοῶ) with certain knowledge (ἐπίσταμαι) and full assurance (πεπληροφόρημαι, perfect passive).
rejected: I don't guess, but I understand and am convinced
I do not imagine, but I know and am certain

choices.english: We hold it as a prayer
choices.why: The idiom δι' εὐχῆς ἔχειν means 'to count as a matter of prayer' or 'to desire earnestly'; Justin frames suffering as something prayed for.
Glossary term; the confidence of the faithful before God's judgment seat.

pass_b_english: The prefect said to Justin, "Hear me, you who are called learned and think you know true arguments: if you are scourged and beheaded, are you persuaded that you are about to go up into heaven?" Justin said, "I hope to have his teachings there, if I endure these things. For I know that the divine gift remains with all who have lived this way until the completion of the whole world." The prefect Rusticus said, "So you suppose that you will go up into the heavens and receive some rewards?" Justin said, "I do not suppose it; I know it and have been fully assured." The prefect Rusticus said, "Let us now come to the matter at hand, which is pressing. Come together with one accord and sacrifice to the gods." Justin said, "No one of sound mind falls from piety into impiety." The prefect Rusticus said, "If you do not obey, you will be punished without mercy." Justin said, "It is our prayer that, having been punished for the sake of our Lord Jesus Christ, we may be saved; for this will be our salvation and boldness before the more fearful and universal tribunal of our Master and Savior." In the same way the remaining martyrs said, "Do what you wish. We are Christians, and we do not sacrifice to idols."

problems.quote: I hope to have his teachings
problems.why: αὐτοῦ refers to heaven's location (there), not a person; 'his teachings' misrepresents the grammar.
problems.fix: I hope to hold those teachings there, if I endure these things.
problems.ruling: αὐτοῦ is adverbial 'there'; τὰ δόγματα are Christian teachings, not 'his teachings' of a person.

edits.old: I hope to have his teachings
edits.new: I hope to have those teachings there

fixed: Mistranslation: 'his teachings' misreads the source 'αὐτοῦ τὰ δόγματα', where 'αὐτοῦ' is adverbial ('there'), not a possessive referring to a person. Changed to 'those teachings there'.

problems.quote: We hold it as a prayer
problems.why: δι' εὐχῆς means 'with prayer' or 'as our prayer/wish', but 'hold it as a prayer' is awkward and obscures that punishment is the means to salvation
problems.fix: It is our prayer that, punished for our Lord Jesus Christ, we may be saved

problems.quote: I hope to have those teachings there
problems.why: αὐτοῦ means 'his' (God's/heaven's), not 'those'; 'teachings' for δόγματα is weak
problems.fix: I hope to possess his teaching there
problems.ruling: αὐτοῦ is genitive 'his/its', not 'those'; ἕξειν αὐτοῦ τὰ δόγματα = 'to have his teachings', not 'those teachings there'

edits.old: I hope to have those teachings there
edits.new: I hope to have his teachings there

edits.old: We hold it as a prayer that, having been punished for the sake of our Lord Jesus Christ, we may be saved
edits.new: It is our prayer that, having been punished for the sake of our Lord Jesus Christ, we may be saved

fixed: Δι' εὐχῆς ἔχομεν means 'we hold it as a prayer' or 'it is our prayer'; the English was awkward and obscured that punishment is the means to salvation.

problems.why: 'Child' in intro vs 'Son' in body; same Greek pais, but reader may think two different Christologies.

variants.text: the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God

problems.quote: In the same way the remaining martyrs said
problems.why: Group speech with no individual markers; reader cannot tell if Justin speaks for all or all speak together.
problems.fix: Note this is a choral response.

problems.quote: No one of sound mind falls from worship into impiety
problems.why: 'Falls from worship' is opposite of expected logic; should be 'falls from piety into impiety.'
problems.fix: 'No one of sound mind turns from piety to impiety'.

edits.old: No one of sound mind falls from worship into impiety.
edits.new: No one of sound mind falls from piety into impiety.

fixed: The glossary issue about 'Child' vs 'Son' is not present in this section; the English here does not use either term, so no edit is needed.
The speaker issue is a stylistic observation, not a mistranslation; the English accurately renders 'Ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ μάρτυρες εἶπον' as a group speech, so no edit is needed.

The mistranslation is real: the source has 'ἀπὸ εὐσεβείας ἀσεβείᾳ εἰσπίπτει' (from piety into impiety), not 'from worship into impiety'. The English 'worship' misstates the source, so I changed it to 'piety'.
